title: The Mahjong Tradition
text:
Traditions connect us. They create reasons to gather, stories to share, and bonds that span generations. For over a century, Mahjong has been one of those powerful traditions.
Born in China in the late 1800s, Mahjong quickly spread from home to home, region to region. More than just a game, it became a way for families, neighbors, and friends to connect.
When Mahjong arrived in America in the 1920s, it found new communities while honoring its roots. Asian American families embraced it as a tie to heritage. Jewish women made it a cornerstone of friendship, passing the tradition from mothers to daughters. Across neighborhoods and living rooms, it carried the same spirit of gathering and joy that defined it from the beginning.
Today, Mahjong continues to bring people together for connection, laughter, and bonds that outlast any single evening at the table.

title: Get to know the tiles
text:
Click through the flashcards below to learn about the different tiles.



There are the five types of Mahjong tiles:

Numbers
Dragons
Winds
Flowers

Numeric Tiles + Dragons
These tiles come in 3 suits: Dots (circles), Bams (bamboo), and Craks (characters). Think of each suit like a playing-card suit—with a “face card” in the form of a Dragon.


Dots

Paired Dragon: White Dragon (often called soap)

title: Game Play
text:
Now that you know the tiles, the deal, the Charleston, and the card—it’s time to actually play the game!

The Flow of a Turn
Each player takes turns in counter-clockwise order, beginning with East. A turn has two main steps:

Draw a Tile

On your turn, you must draw one tile.

You can draw from the wall (the normal stack of tiles) OR call a discard if it completes a set for your hand.

Discard a Tile

After drawing, you must discard one tile face-up into the center.

Your hand always returns to 13 tiles (or 14 if you’re declaring Mahjong).




Calling Discards
When someone discards a tile, other players have the chance to call it:

Pung/Kong/Quint: If the discard completes your set of 3, 4, or 5 identical tiles, you can call immediately.

Mahjong!: If the discard gives you a complete hand from the card, you can declare Mahjong and win the round.

Priority: If multiple players want the same discard, the one declaring Mahjong always takes priority. Otherwise, the player closest in turn order to the discarder gets it.


Pro tip: You can only call for a pair if it completes a winning Mahjong hand. Otherwise, pairs must be drawn naturally.



Winning a Hand
To declare Mahjong, your hand must:

Match exactly one of the combinations shown on the card

Contain 14 tiles (13 plus the winning tile)

Once you win, you lay down your tiles for all players to see and the hand ends.


Ending Without a Winner
If all tiles in the wall are used up before anyone declares Mahjong, the round ends in a wall game. Players reset and start a new hand, rotating the dealer position (East).

title: Setup and Seating
section: The Four Winds Around Your Table
text:
The Four Winds Around Your Table
American Mahjong is played by four players, each representing one of the cardinal wind directions.
East - The dealer and starting position
South - Sits to East’s right
West - Sits across from East
North - Sits to East’s left
Fun Fact: The wind seating doesn’t follow a traditional compass layout. In Mahjong, the winds follow Asian cardinal points and have traditional associations with seasons (East/Spring, South/Summer, West/Autumn, North/Winter), which may explain why the arrangement differs from a standard compass.














The wind positions rotate throughout the game, giving each player a turn as the dealer. Don’t worry about memorizing everything now, we’ll cover the significance of these positions as we progress through the lessons.

title: The Card
text:
The American Mahjong card is your guide to winning hands. You can purchase this year’s official card from the National Mah Jongg League. Each line shows exactly what 14 tiles you need to win, using shorthand symbols and helpful notes.



Basic Structure
Every line on the card represents one complete winning hand. The card is organized into different categories, and each hand shows:

Shorthand notation (the tile abbreviations)
Notes (additional details about requirements)
Point values (how much the hand is worth)
Concealed (whether the hand must be concealed, incidated by a C)




Shorthand
The card uses these standard abbreviations:

1-9: Numbered tiles (any suit: dots, bams, or craks)
D: Dragon
0: Soap (white dragon, can be paired with any suit)
N, E, W, S: Wind tiles (North, East, West, South)
F: Flower tiles



Examples
11 22 333 444 5555
This means you need 2 ones, 2 twos, 3 threes, 3 fours, and 4 fives
FFFF 11 22 333 DDD
This means you need 4 flowers, 2 ones, 2 twos, 3 threes, and 3 dragons



Essential Vocabulary
Understanding these terms is crucial for reading the card:

Pair: 2 identical tiles
Pung: 3 identical tiles

Kong: 4 identical tiles
Quint: 5 identical tiles




Reading the Notes
The notes next to each line give you critical information:
Suit Requirements

“Same suit” = All numbered tiles must be from the same suit
“Any 3 suits” = Use tiles from exactly 3 different suits
“2 suits” = Use tiles from exactly 2 suits

Special Conditions

“X” = The pungs (sets of 3), kongs (sets of 4), or quints (sets of 5) can be called from the discards
“C” = Conceled. NO tiles cannot be called from discards
“Consecutive numbers” = Numbers must be in order (like 1-2-3)



Example
FFFF 11 22 333 DDD (Any 3 Consec. Nos. with Matching Dragons)
This means you do not need exactly 11 22 333, but you can use any 3 consecutive numbers (i.e. 44 55 666 or 77 88 999 would also work!). The dragons must match the suit, (i.e. if you numbers are all bams, you must use the green dragons, if your numbers are all craks you must use the red dragon, if your numbers are all dots you must use the white dragon (soap!)).




Color Coding
When numbered tiles appear in the same color on the card, they must all be from the same suit.
Different colors mean you must have different suits for those tiles.
This visual system helps you quickly identify suit requirements at a glance.


Example
22 44 44 666 8888 (Any 3 Suits)
This means that the suit for the 22 and 44 must match, the suit for the 44 666 must match (and be different from the 22 44 suit), and the 8888 must be in the third suit.



Common Card Sections
The hands are grouped into sections that appear year after year:
{Year}: Hands using the current year with numbered tiles and soaps (e.g. 2025)
2468: Hands with only even numbers
Any Like Numbers: All numbers are the same (e.g., all 3s)
Math Sections: Some cards include multiplication/addition themes (e.g., FF 1111 + 6666 = 7777)
Quints: Hands including 5-of-a-kind groupings
Consecutive Runs: Numbers in increasing order (e.g., 1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
13579: Hands with only odd numbers
Winds and Dragons: Hands featuring mostly winds and dragons
369: Hands using the numbers 3, 6, and 9
Singles and Pairs: Hands with only single tiles and pairs


How to Use the Card

Pick a category that matches tiles you’re collecting
Read the shorthand to see what tiles you need
Check the notes for specific requirements
Count to 14 to verify it’s a complete hand

The combination of shorthand + notes tells you exactly what you need to win!






← Previous


Next →



Pro tip: Make sure to read the notes! Sometimes the pattern will use one number, but the notes specify that multiple numbers qualify.

title: The Charleston
text:
After the tiles are dealt, the game begins with a Charleston - a series of tile exchanges between players. Each Charleston consists of three passes, with each player passing exactly 3 tiles during each pass.
The final pass of a Charleston can be a blind pass. Instead of selecting 3 tiles from your hand, you can choose 0, 1, or 2 tiles from your own collection and complete the set of 3 by including tiles you just received from another player (without looking at them first).
If all players agree, you can complete two full Charlestons before starting the main game. The order of the passes are:
First Charleston: Right → Across → Left
Second Charleston: Left → Across → Right
After the Charleston(s), players may make an optional courtesy pass with the player sitting across from them. Both players must agree on how many tiles to exchange (0-3 tiles each). Either player can decline to pass any tiles.


Practice the Charleston:
Select 3 tiles to pass each time. Drag the tiles to the correct player.
First Charleston: Right → Across → Left
Second Charleston: Left → Across → Right
Blind passes can be made on the 2nd Left and 2rd Right.

This Privacy Policy explains how Magic Mahjong Moments (“we,” “us,” or “our”) collects, uses, discloses, and protects personal information in connection with the Magic Mahjong Moments online storefront (the “Site”). By using the Site or placing an order you agree to the collection and use of information in accordance with this policy.



This policy covers information collected through the Site only. It does not apply to information collected directly by third parties (for example, payment processors or shipping carriers) except as described below.






When you place an order we collect the billing and shipping information required to fulfill that order, such as name, delivery address, billing address, and phone number if provided at checkout. We collect only the information necessary to process and ship your order.



We do not collect or store full payment card details. All payment transactions are processed by Stripe. Any payment card details or other payment-specific information are provided directly to and stored by Stripe in accordance with their systems and policies. We may receive confirmation of payment and basic payment metadata (e.g., transaction ID, last 4 digits, payment status) from Stripe to manage your order.



When you visit the Site we may automatically collect certain technical information about your device and use of the Site, including IP address, browser type, operating system, pages visited, referring URLs, and other diagnostic and usage data. This information is collected through server logs and cookies and is used to operate and improve the Site.



We and third-party services we use may place cookies, pixels, and similar technologies on your device. These help with site functionality, fraud prevention, performance measurement, and analytics. You may control cookie settings through your browser, but disabling certain cookies may affect Site functionality.





We use the information we collect for the following purposes:

To process and fulfill orders (billing, shipping, order confirmations and order history).
To process refunds, exchanges, and cancellations.
To investigate and prevent fraud, abuse, or other prohibited uses.
To operate, maintain, and improve the Site and our services (including troubleshooting, data analysis and testing).
To comply with legal obligations (for example, tax or recordkeeping requirements).

We do not use personal data for marketing communications from Magic Mahjong Moments unless you explicitly opt into a separate communication channel that you set up via the Site (the Site does not collect or retain a customer mailing list by default).




We may share information with:

Service providers and vendors. Third parties that perform services on our behalf (payment processors such as Stripe, shipping carriers, fulfillment centers, fraud-prevention providers, hosting and analytics services). These parties are contractually limited to using data only as necessary to provide their services.
Legal and safety. When required by law or in response to lawful requests by public authorities, or to protect the rights, property, or safety of Magic Mahjong Moments, our customers, or others.
Business transfers. In connection with a merger, acquisition, sale of assets, financing, or similar transaction involving Magic Mahjong Moments, personal information may be transferred as part of that transaction.

We do not sell personal information.




The Site may contain links to third-party websites and may use third-party services (for example Stripe, shipping carriers, analytics providers). Those services operate under their own privacy policies and terms. We are not responsible for their practices. Payment processing and related records are governed by the payment processor’s policies.




We retain personal information for as long as necessary to provide the Site and our services, to comply with our legal obligations, to resolve disputes, and to enforce our agreements. Order and transaction records are retained for tax and accounting purposes for a period required by law. Non-identifying, aggregated analytics data may be retained indefinitely.




We use administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to protect personal information appropriate to the nature of the data. However, no internet-based system is completely secure. If you believe your order or payment information has been compromised, contact us via the Site contact form and provide relevant order details so we can investigate.




The Site is not directed to children under 16. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 16. If you believe we have collected data from a child in violation of this policy, contact us so we can delete the information.




The Site is operated from the United States (North Carolina). If you access the Site from outside the United States, your information may be transferred to, processed, and stored in the United States. By using the Site and providing information, you consent to such transfers. If you are located in a jurisdiction with data-transfer restrictions, please contact us through the Site contact form to discuss.




Subject to applicable law, you may have the right to:

Access the personal information we hold about you.
Request correction of inaccurate or incomplete information.
Request deletion of personal information (unless retention is required for legal or business purposes).
Object to or restrict certain processing.
Request a copy of your personal information in a portable format.

To exercise these rights, submit a request via the Site contact form and include enough information for us to identify your order or records (for example, order number and date). We may need to verify your identity before responding. We will respond to requests in accordance with applicable law.




We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. When we do, we will post the revised policy with a new effective date. Continued use of the Site after posting constitutes acceptance of the revised policy.




To ask questions about this Privacy Policy or to exercise your rights, please use the contact form on the Site and include relevant order details or the nature of your request. We will respond using the channel you provide through the contact form.

By using the Site you acknowledge that you have read and understood this Privacy Policy.
